regles.armeMaisonNeedsVariante: Choose a variant first ("Active rules" button) — a created rule never touches an official base.
regles.creerArmeMaisonVariante: This weapon will be added to your variant "{name}".
regles.descriptionDeLArme: Description (optional — copy the text from your own source)
regles.descriptionLibreArmeExemple: e.g. A longsword deals 1d8 slashing, 1d10 if wielded two-handed.
regles.propositionEchouee: The model did not produce a valid structure — fill in the form manually.
regles.erreurServiceIA: Could not reach the local AI provider — try again or fill in the form manually.

regles.historiqueMaisonNeedsVariante: Choose a variant first ("Active rules" button) — a created rule never touches an official base.
regles.creerHistoriqueMaisonVariante: This background will be added to your variant "{name}".
regles.creerHistoriqueMaisonIntro: Copy the values from your own source (nothing here is guessed) — three different abilities, the skill proficiencies, the starting equipment, and the granted feat.
regles.descriptionDeLHistorique: Description (optional — copy the text from your own source)
regles.descriptionDuDon: Feat description (copy the text from your source)
regles.erreurDonInconnu: Pick an existing feat from the list.
regles.erreurCreationHistorique: Could not create this background — try again.
regles.donMaisonNeedsVariante: Choose a variant first ("Active rules" button) — a created rule never touches an official base.
regles.creerDonMaisonVariante: This feat will be added to your variant "{name}".
regles.creerDonMaisonIntro: Copy the values from your own source (nothing here is guessed). The numeric effects below (ability score, saving throw, skill, AC, speed, hit points) really apply to the character sheet — everything else (a conditional reroll, a situational advantage…) stays as described text, applied at your table like official feats of the same kind (Lucky, Indomitable…).
regles.effetsChiffresAide: Only for effects that truly match one of these targets — everything else about the feat belongs in the text above.
regles.creerSousClasseVariante: This subclass will be added to your variant “{name}” — {origin}.
regles.origineReferencePersonnelle: a personal reference: enter only the mechanics, never a book's prose
regles.creerSousClasseIntro: Copy the values from your own source (nothing is guessed here). For a book's text, give its page instead of copying it: you have the book at hand at the table.
regles.aucuneClasse: No class in the active variant: create or import a class first.
regles.aptitudesDeSousClasseAide: One line per feature, with the level it is gained at. At least one named feature.
regles.descriptionDeLAptitude: What it does, in a few words (or its page)
regles.erreurCreationSousClasse: The subclass could not be created.
regles.sousClasseSansEmplacement: Subclass created. Its class has no subclass slot: it won't be offered at character creation until the class has one.
regles.erreurCreationDon: Could not create this feat — try again.
regles.bacASableDescription: Test a formula with the same engine as the real game — dice are rolled server-side.
regles.erreurEvaluationFormule: Could not evaluate this formula — check the syntax.
regles.referencePersonnelleOption: Personal reference — content entered from a book I own
regles.referencePersonnelleAvertissement: This content stays within your private play circle: never a share link, an export, or a switch to an ordinary homebrew rule — your players consult it in session, without ever leaving with a copy.
regles.referencePersonnelleFicheTitre: This entry comes from a personal-reference ruleset — private play circle only, never shared or exported.
regles.bacASableDeclencheursDescription: Try a rule without touching a game. The same engine as real play: dice are rolled by the server.
regles.erreurSimulation: Simulation failed — check the trigger's shape.
regles.declencheursIntro: What happens when an event occurs in play. Simple rules go here; a complex rule (a saving throw with its failure branch) is composed in the trigger sandbox.
regles.declencheurIncomplet: A trigger is incomplete: it will not be saved.
